literal: He prayed for rain without effect and then whipped the image a hundred strokes.
idiomatic: The prayer failed; he whipped the image a hundred strokes.

literal: That month a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died.
idiomatic: That month a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died.

literal: Posthumous title Hui; a thousand bolts of silk were given, and at the burial another thousand bolts, with a Yellow Gate Gentleman to oversee the rites.
idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Prince Hui; a thousand bolts of silk were granted, and at burial another thousand, with a Yellow Gate Gentleman to oversee the rites.

literal: When Hengzhou Inspector Mu Tai plotted rebellion, Zhen knew and did not report; though already dead, his title was still posthumously stripped and the fief abolished.
idiomatic: When Hengzhou inspector Mu Tai rebelled, Zhen knew and did not report; though dead, his title was posthumously stripped and the fief abolished.

literal: He had five sons.
idiomatic: He had five sons.

literal: Ying, Prince Xianwu of Zhongshan
idiomatic: Ying, Prince Xianwu of Zhongshan

literal: His son Ying, styled Hu'er.
idiomatic: His son Ying, courtesy name Hu'er.

literal: By nature he was clever and keen in perception, broadly learned with a strong memory, skilled at bow and horse, able to play the flute, and slightly versed in medicine.
idiomatic: Clever and keen, broadly learned with a strong memory, he was skilled at bow and horse, could play the flute, and knew a little medicine.

literal: Under Gaozu he was made General Who Pacifies the North, Grand General of Wuchuan Garrison, and Acting Duke of Wei.
idiomatic: Under Gaozu he was General Who Pacifies the North, commander of Wuchuan Garrison, and Acting Duke of Wei.

literal: Before long he was transferred to commander of all military affairs of Liang, Yi, and Ning, General Who Pacifies the South, Protector-General of the Western Rong, Grand General of Chouchi Garrison, and Inspector of Liangzhou.
idiomatic: Soon he was made commander of armies in Liang, Yi, and Ning, General Who Pacifies the South, Protector-General of the Western Rong, commander of Chouchi Garrison, and inspector of Liangzhou.

literal: When Gaozu campaigned south he was commander of the separate route through Liang and Han.
idiomatic: On Gaozu's southern campaign he commanded the separate Liang-Han column.

literal: Later, when the imperial carriage reached Zhongli, an edict ordered Ying to lead troops and guard the border.
idiomatic: When the imperial carriage reached Zhongli, an edict ordered Ying to guard the frontier with his troops.

literal: Ying, because the imperial carriage moved in person and momentum tilted toward the southeast, saw that Hanzhong offered an opening, memorialized asking to advance and attack, and Gaozu approved.
idiomatic: Seeing the emperor advance in person and momentum pour toward the southeast, Ying judged Hanzhong open, asked to strike, and Gaozu agreed.

literal: The army halted at the Ju River; Xiao Luan's general Xiao Yi sent Yin Shaozu, Liang Jiqun, and others with twenty thousand men to take the mountains and raise palisades in several places, looking down from the heights and making camps across the water.
idiomatic: The army halted at the Ju River. Xiao Yi's general Xiao Yi sent Yin Shaozu and Liang Jiqun with twenty thousand men to seize the heights, raise palisades in several places, and camp across the water looking down.

literal: Ying then counseled: "Their commanders despise the people and are arrogant; none can make the rest obey. Many men without a head—they do not know whom to follow.
idiomatic: Ying counseled, "Their leaders despise the men and cannot command them. A host without a head does not know whom to follow.

literal: If we choose crack troops and together strike one camp, they will not rescue one another and we are sure to take them.
idiomatic: Choose crack troops and strike one camp together—they will not aid one another and we are sure to win.

literal: If we take one army, the four camps will pull themselves up of themselves.
idiomatic: Break one camp and the other four will collapse of themselves."

literal: " Thereupon he picked troops and charged up on three sides; indeed they did not rescue one another.
idiomatic: He picked troops and charged on three sides; as he foresaw, they did not aid one another.

literal: Once one place was broken, all four camps collapsed; Liang Jiqun was taken alive, more than three thousand were beheaded, and seven hundred captured.
idiomatic: One position fell and all four camps broke; Liang Jiqun was taken alive, more than three thousand beheaded, seven hundred captured.

literal: Luan's White Horse Garrison general fled in the night and dissolved.
idiomatic: Luan's garrison at White Horse fled in the night and dissolved.

literal: Pressing the victory in a long drive, he was about to close on Nanzheng; the people of Hanzhong took him for a god and came in succession to submit.
idiomatic: Pressing the victory he drove toward Nanzheng; the people of Hanzhong took him for a god and submitted in waves.

literal: Liangzhou man Li Tian'gan and others came to Ying to surrender and were treated with the rites due a champion of the state.
idiomatic: Li Tian'gan of Liangzhou and others surrendered to Ying and were treated as champions of the state.

literal: Tian'gan and the rest had families west of Nanzheng and asked troops to welcome them; Ying sent men to welcome them.
idiomatic: Tian'gan's kin lay west of Nanzheng; he asked for troops to fetch them, and Ying sent escorts.

literal: Xiao Yi heard and sent General Jiang Xiu with troops to pursue and strike; at night they fought and there were considerable casualties.
idiomatic: Xiao Yi heard and sent Jiang Xiu in pursuit; they fought at night with heavy casualties.

literal: Xiu afterward was repeatedly defeated and again asked for troops.
idiomatic: Xiu was beaten again and again and asked for more troops.

literal: Yi sent troops to go; the welcomers reported urgency.
idiomatic: Yi sent reinforcements; the escort party cried urgent need.

literal: Ying led a thousand horse and went by double marches to rescue.
idiomatic: Ying led a thousand horse at double march to rescue them.

literal: Before he arrived the bandits had already retreated.
idiomatic: Before he arrived the enemy had already withdrawn.

literal: Ying feared they would enter the city; he separately sent the commandery general Yuan Ba to follow behind them while Ying intercepted before them and struck together, capturing the whole host.
idiomatic: Fearing they would enter the city, he sent Commandery General Yuan Ba to follow behind while he himself blocked the front; together they took the whole force.

literal: Yi continued to send troops; Ying did not expect the bandits to arrive, and as his force was already weary and few, the men were afraid and all wished to flee.
idiomatic: Yi sent more troops; Ying did not expect them, his men were weary and few, and all wished to run.

literal: Ying then slowed his horse and advanced at ease, his expression calm; he climbed high to view the bandits, pointing and commanding east and west as if disposing troops, then arrayed the ranks and went forward.
idiomatic: Ying slowed his horse, face calm, climbed high to view the enemy, gestured east and west as if disposing troops, then re-formed ranks and advanced.

literal: The bandits thought there were ambush troops.
idiomatic: The enemy thought ambush lay in wait.

literal: Soon the bandits retreated; pressing the momentum he pursued and destroyed them, then besieged Nanzheng.
idiomatic: Soon they withdrew; he pursued, destroyed them, and besieged Nanzheng.

literal: He forbade the three armies from a single violation; near and far all supplied grain transport.
idiomatic: He forbade his three armies every violation; near and far the people brought grain.

literal: Earlier, before Ying had arrived, Xiao Yi had sent the army commander Fan Jie with more than three thousand men to attack the Liao.
idiomatic: Before Ying arrived, Xiao Yi had sent Army Commander Fan Jie with more than three thousand men against the Liao.

literal: Jie heard the great army besieged the city and wished to return to rescue.
idiomatic: Jie heard the great army had besieged the city and turned back to rescue it.

literal: Ying sent the commandery generals Li Pingdi and Li Tieqi and others to gather the men of Baxi and Jinshou and cut his road.
idiomatic: Ying sent Li Pingdi, Li Tieqi, and others to rally men of Baxi and Jinshou and cut Jie's road.

literal: Jie fought to the death and thereupon defeated Pingdi's army.
idiomatic: Jie fought to the death and broke Pingdi's force.

literal: Ying waited until they drew somewhat near, then with odd troops masked them and captured them all.
idiomatic: Ying waited until they drew near, then ambushed and took them all.

literal: The siege lasted more than ninety days; in battle nothing failed.
idiomatic: The siege ran more than ninety days; every assault succeeded.

literal: He received orders to withdraw the army.
idiomatic: Orders came to withdraw.

literal: Ying thereupon first sent off the old and weak, himself led crack troops to remain behind, and sent a messenger to take leave of Yi.
idiomatic: Ying first sent off the old and weak, kept crack troops in the rear himself, and sent a messenger to bid Yi farewell.

literal: Yi thought it a trick; one day after Ying had gone he still did not open the gates.
idiomatic: Yi thought it a ruse; a full day after Ying left the gates stayed shut.

literal: Two days afterward Yi then sent a general to pursue Ying.
idiomatic: Two days later Yi sent a general in pursuit.

literal: Ying himself brought up the rear and dismounted with the soldiers to fight hand to hand; the bandit host dared not press him.
idiomatic: Ying brought up the rear himself, fought dismounted with his men, and the enemy dared not press close.

literal: Four days and four nights, and then the bandits withdrew; the whole army returned intact.
idiomatic: For four days and four nights the enemy hung back; then they withdrew and the whole army returned intact.

literal: Just then the mountain Di all rebelled and cut Ying's road of return.
idiomatic: Just then the mountain Di rebelled and cut his road home.

literal: Ying drove the host in fierce attack, fighting as he marched; he was struck by a stray arrow, and the soldiers did not know it.
idiomatic: He drove his men in fierce attack, fighting as he marched; a stray arrow struck him, and none knew.

literal: For merit he was transferred to Grand General Who Pacifies the South and granted the rank Baron of Guangwu.
idiomatic: For merit he was made Grand General Who Pacifies the South and Baron of Guangwu.

literal: Six years at Chouchi; he had a great name for authority and kindness.
idiomatic: Six years at Chouchi won him a great name for stern kindness.

literal: His father's mourning; he resigned his post.
idiomatic: At his father's death he resigned.

literal: Later Ying returned to the capital and submitted a memorial: "Your servant has heard that taking disorder and repenting ruin is a state's constant way;
idiomatic: Later, back in the capital, he memorialized: "I have heard that seizing disorder and repenting ruin is a state's constant way;

literal: arraying troops and mustering hosts is to strike as opportunity offers.
idiomatic: arraying troops is to strike when opportunity offers.

literal: I venture to think that petty Baojuan, heedless of heaven's constant, relies on mountains and rivers and dares resist the Middle Kingdom.
idiomatic: I venture that petty Baojuan, heedless of heaven's law, trusts his mountains and rivers and dares resist the Middle Kingdom.

literal: Now the demon rebels are several times destroyed, arrogance and license grow daily, he insults the Five Agents, neglects the Three Alignments, uses cruel punishments to his heart's content, and harms the innocent.
idiomatic: His rebels are several times broken, yet arrogance grows daily; he insults the Five Agents, neglects the calendar, tortures at will, and harms the innocent.

literal: His Inspector of Yongzhou, Xiao Yan, eastward attacks Moling, sweeps the land and raises troops, flows down the river—and there is only a lone city, no second guard.
idiomatic: His Yongzhou inspector Xiao Yan attacks Moling eastward, sweeps the land, raises troops, and drifts downriver—leaving only a lone city without a second guard.

literal: This is the day heaven grants us, the autumn met once in vast ages; the affair is easy as rolling a pellet, the principle like picking up a mustard seed—if we do not ride this, what shall we wait for?
idiomatic: This is the day heaven grants us, an autumn that comes once in vast ages; the task is easy as rolling a pellet, simple as plucking a mustard seed—if we do not ride this moment, what shall we wait for?

literal: Your servant begs to lead thirty thousand foot and horse in person straight to the Mian's north, hold the city of Xiangyang, and cut the Black Water road.
idiomatic: I beg to lead thirty thousand foot and horse straight to the north bank of the Mian, hold Xiangyang, and cut the Black Water road.

literal: The benighted and cruel ruler and ministers will devour one another like fish.
idiomatic: Their benighted ruler and ministers will devour one another like fish.

literal: We hold the upper stream, our authority shaking far and near; a long drive southward will advance to take Jiangling.
idiomatic: Holding the upper stream we shake the far reaches; a long drive south will seize Jiangling.

literal: The road is near, not five hundred li; then the land of the Three Chu may be gathered in one morning, and the road to Min and Shu will of itself be cut.
idiomatic: The road is near—less than five hundred li—then the Three Chu may fall in a morning and the road to Min and Shu will cut itself off.

literal: Also order Yang and Xu provinces to proclaim that both will rise together, burn along the river, and leave nothing behind.
idiomatic: Order Yang and Xu to proclaim a joint rising, burn along the river, and leave nothing behind.

literal: Jianye will be cornered, a fish in the cauldron.
idiomatic: Jianye will be cornered—a fish in the cauldron.

literal: The army of a well-governed state will rise again, Sun Hao's bonds will come once more, the text and wheel will be made one, heaven and earth mixed into one.
idiomatic: The army of a well-governed state will rise again, Sun Hao's bonds will return, the text and wheel will be one, heaven and earth merged.

literal: I bow and consider that Your Majesty will for a time set aside the imperial capstrings, slightly incline your ear, decide in your sage heart alone without taking doubtful counsel—if this term slips away, the day of swallowing whole is not yet come.
idiomatic: I bow and beg Your Majesty to set aside the capstrings awhile, incline your ear, decide in your sage heart without doubtful counsel—if this season slips away, the day of swallowing whole is not yet here."

literal: The affair was shelved without reply.
idiomatic: The memorial was shelved without reply.

literal: Ying again memorialized: "Your servant has heard that striking the weak by void, the affair lies in swift raising; attacking the obscure by peril, sudden merit may be expected.
idiomatic: Ying memorialized again: "I hear that striking weakness through void lies in swift action; attacking peril through obscurity promises sudden merit.

literal: Now Baojuan disorders the constant; bone and flesh harm one another; frontier garrisons stand like tripods and none knows where to turn.
idiomatic: Now Baojuan disorders the constant; kin turn on kin; frontier garrisons stand like tripods and none knows where to turn.

literal: Yiyang stands isolated, close to our heavenly border; without grain support from outside, within it has no store of arms.
idiomatic: Yiyang stands alone, close to our border; without grain from outside, within it has no arms store.

literal: This is a bird facing the blaze—one cannot remove the fuel;
idiomatic: This is a bird facing the blaze—you cannot remove the fuel;

literal: a foe offering his head—how can the axe be slow?
idiomatic: a foe offering his head—how can the axe be slow?

literal: If this march has fruit, then the lands right of the river will be the base of further planning;
idiomatic: If this march succeeds, the lands south of the river become the base of further planning;

literal: if it misses, not only will later efforts be hard to plot, but perhaps even in peace sickness will grow.
idiomatic: if it fails, later efforts grow hard—and even in peace sickness may grow.

literal: [1]Now Inspector of Yuzhou Sima Yue has already ordered alert and is about to march, while Inspector of East Yuzhou Tian Yizong is just planning to hold the Three Passes—please send a army supervisor to command them.
idiomatic: [1]Inspector of Yuzhou Sima Yue has already ordered alert and is about to march, while East Yuzhou inspector Tian Yizong plans to hold the Three Passes—please send an army supervisor to command them.

literal: " Shizong sent the Direct Attendant Yang Lingyin as army supervisor.
idiomatic: Shizong sent Direct Attendant Yang Lingyin as army supervisor.

literal: For military merit he was appointed Minister of the Masters of Writing; for successive military achievements he was advanced to Marquis of Changshan.
idiomatic: For military merit he was made Minister of the Masters of Writing; for further victories he was advanced to Marquis of Changshan.

literal: Ying memorialized: "According to the school ordinance: students of the various provinces and commanderies are once every three years examined on the classics they have mastered, listed by the regular envoy, and then an envoy is sent to the commandery to drill and examine.
idiomatic: Ying memorialized: "According to the school ordinance, provincial students are every three years examined on classics mastered, listed by the regular envoy, then an envoy drills and examines in the commandery.

literal: Your servant bows and considers the sage brightness, exalting the Way and displaying the wind of the accomplished academy, storing righteousness and shining the beauty of the glue-and-lacquer sequence—therefore the Grand Academy's halls were long set in the lower states, and the Four Gates' teaching was just then built at the capital ford.
idiomatic: I bow before sage brightness that exalts the Way, displays the academy's wind, stores righteousness, and shines the glue-and-lacquer schools—therefore the Grand Academy stood long in the provinces and the Four Gates were just raised at the capital ford.

literal: I reckon that training and study run over years, hearing and receiving may span many cycles, yet the outstanding stream should be questioned at the Wei gate, and the unaltered remainder should return to the common folk—let them undergo commandery drill and examination and verify the highest and lowest.
idiomatic: Training runs years, study many cycles—yet the outstanding should be questioned at the Wei gate and the unfit returned to the people, examined in the commanderies and ranked highest to lowest.

literal: Recently, because the imperial capital was moved and Jiang and Yang were not yet one, the commandery schools' instruction could not attend to the regular trial.
idiomatic: Recently, with the capital moved and Jiang and Yang not yet one, commandery schools could not hold the regular trial.

literal: It has caused the quality of wormwood and artemisia to be equally taught in the school court;
idiomatic: Wormwood and artemisia alike sit in the school court;

literal: orchid and mugwort alike receive instruction in the literary stalls.
idiomatic: orchid and mugwort alike are taught in the literary stalls.

literal: Now the outer prefects and capital officials have finished their review appointments; I ask to send Four Gates academicians clear in the Five Classics to examine separately by the Way and, according to the ordinance, promote and demote.
idiomatic: Outer prefects and capital officials have finished review; I ask to send Four Gates doctors versed in the Five Classics to examine by the Way and promote or demote by ordinance.

literal: " An edict said: "Scholarly work has long lain in ruin—not one envoy can urge it; presently there will be a separate decree."
idiomatic: The edict answered, "Scholarly work has lain in ruin for long—not one envoy can restore it; a separate decree will follow."

literal: Soon an edict made Ying Bearer of the Staff, Acting General Who Pacifies the South, and commander of all armies campaigning on Yiyang, leading troops south to attack.
idiomatic: Soon he was made Bearer of the Staff, Acting General Who Pacifies the South, commander of armies on Yiyang, and led troops south.

literal: Xiao Yan's Inspector of Sizhou, Cai Daogong, heard Ying was coming and sent his fierce-cavalry general Yang You to lead more than three thousand households of residents outside the city to Xianshou Mountain ten li southwest of the city, taking the ridge to make three palisades in an inner-outer disposition.
idiomatic: Xiao Yan's Sizhou inspector Cai Daogong heard Ying was coming and sent Fierce-Cavalry General Yang You with more than three thousand households from outside the city to Xianshou Mountain ten li southwest, where they took the ridge for three palisades in inner-outer array.

literal: Ying drove the armies to besiege the Xianshou stronghold and burned the palisade gates.
idiomatic: Ying besieged the Xianshou stronghold and burned the palisade gates.

literal: Yang You then drove water buffalo out of the camp, with troops following.
idiomatic: Yang You drove water buffalo from the camp with troops behind.

literal: The soldiers avoided the buffalo and the army thereupon withdrew downhill.
idiomatic: Soldiers dodged the buffalo and the army fell back downhill.

literal: Soon he divided troops to surround and hold them.
idiomatic: Soon he divided troops to surround and hold them.

literal: That night the palisade man Ren Maju beheaded You and surrendered.
idiomatic: That night the palisade man Ren Maju beheaded You and surrendered.

literal: The three armies were quartered on grain; the surrendered people were settled in peace.
idiomatic: The three armies fed on captured grain; the surrendered people were settled in peace.

literal: Xiao Yan sent his General Who Pacifies the West, Cao Jingzong, and Rear General Wang Sengbing and others with thirty thousand foot and horse to rescue Yiyang.
idiomatic: Xiao Yan sent General Who Pacifies the West Cao Jingzong and Rear General Wang Sengbing with thirty thousand foot and horse to rescue Yiyang.

literal: Sengbing commanded twenty thousand and held Zao Pass; Jingzong led ten thousand and followed after.
idiomatic: Sengbing held Zao Pass with twenty thousand; Jingzong followed with ten thousand.

literal: Ying sent the Champion General Yuan Cheng and the Yanglie General Cao Wenjing forward to hold Fancheng against them.
idiomatic: Ying sent Champion General Yuan Cheng and Yanglie General Cao Wenjing to hold Fancheng against them.

literal: Ying arrayed his officers and men, attacked from corner to corner, and greatly defeated Sengbing's army, capturing and beheading more than four thousand.
idiomatic: Ying arrayed his men, attacked corner to corner, and broke Sengbing's army, capturing or killing more than four thousand.

literal: Ying again built a stronghold on Shiya Mountain to oppose Jingzong, separately sending the various commanders to lie in ambush on the four mountains and show weakness.
idiomatic: He built a camp on Shiya Mountain against Jingzong, sent commanders to ambush on four mountains, and feigned weakness.

literal: Yan's general Ma Xianzun led more than ten thousand men to mask Ying's camp.
idiomatic: Yan's general Ma Xianzun led more than ten thousand to strike Ying's camp.

literal: Ying ordered the armies to feign a northward retreat to lure them; once they reached level ground, Commandery General Fu Yong and three armies struck them and the bandits at once fled.
idiomatic: Ying feigned retreat north to lure them; on level ground Commandery General Fu Yong and three armies struck and the enemy fled at once.

literal: Pressing the attack he routed them, beheading more than two thousand three hundred, and beheading the bandits' Forest Guard supervisor Deng Zhongnian.
idiomatic: Pressing the attack he routed them, beheading more than two thousand three hundred and killing the enemy Forest Guard supervisor Deng Zhongnian.
